title: Section 28
commentary:
Section 28 specifies the deductions allowable in respect of premises, machinery, plant, or furniture used for the purposes of a business or profession. Under sub-section (1), an assessee can deduct insurance premiums paid against the risk of damage or destruction of these assets. For business premises, deductions extend to land revenue, local rates, and municipal taxes paid, as well as rent paid where the assessee occupies the premises as a tenant. Repair expenses are also deductible provided they are not capital in nature: an occupant otherwise than as a tenant may deduct current repairs to the premises, whereas a tenant may deduct the cost of repairs only if they have undertaken to bear such costs. Similarly, current repairs to machinery, plant, or furniture are deductible so long as they do not constitute capital expenditure.

Sub-section (2) addresses proportionate deductions. Where any premises, building, machinery, plant, or furniture is used only partly, or not wholly and exclusively, for business or professional purposes, the deduction permitted under sub-section (1) is restricted to a fair proportionate amount determined by the Assessing Officer based on its business usage.

Interpretation: The contrast between 'current repairs' for owner-occupants under clause (d) and 'cost of repairs' for tenants under clause (e) implies that tenant repair claims require an explicit agreement or obligation to bear the repair costs.

example.assumptions: All figures are illustrative assumptions: rent paid for office premises is ₹1,20,000; municipal taxes paid are ₹10,000; current revenue repairs to office plant are ₹20,000; the plant is used 75% for business and 25% for personal purposes.
example.scenario: A consultant occupies an office as a tenant, paying annual rent and municipal taxes. During the year, the consultant also incurs repair expenses on specialized plant equipment kept on the premises, which is used partially for professional client work and partially for personal tasks.
example.walkthrough: Under Section 28(1)(c), the full rent of ₹1,20,000 is deductible as the premises are occupied as a tenant for professional purposes. Under Section 28(1)(b), municipal taxes paid of ₹10,000 are deductible. For the plant repairs of ₹20,000, Section 28(1)(f) recognizes current repairs not of a capital nature; however, because the plant is not wholly and exclusively used for the profession, Section 28(2) applies. The Assessing Officer restricts the ₹20,000 plant repair deduction to a fair proportionate share based on usage (75%), resulting in an allowable deduction of ₹15,000.
example.takeaway: Expenses eligible under Section 28 are restricted to a fair proportionate share if the underlying asset is not wholly and exclusively used for business or professional purposes.

mcqs.question: Under Section 28(1)(e), what condition must be satisfied for a tenant to claim a deduction for the cost of repairs to premises?
options: The assessee must have undertaken to bear the cost of repairs, and the amount must not be capital expenditure.
The expenditure must be certified by the local municipal authority as structural work.
The landlord must formally reimburse half the cost to the tenant before filing.
The cost of repairs must exceed the annual rent paid for the premises.
mcqs.explanation: Section 28(1)(e) permits a deduction for the cost of repairs, not being in the nature of capital expenditure, when the premises are occupied by the assessee as a tenant and where he has undertaken to bear the cost of repairs. The other options introduce requirements not present in the statute.

mcqs.question: Which expense is allowable under Section 28(1)(d) when premises are occupied by the assessee otherwise than as a tenant?
options: Capital expenditure incurred on structural enlargement of the building.
Amount paid on account of current repairs to the premises, not being capital expenditure.
Notional rent calculated based on prevailing local market rates.
Insurance premium paid against loss of personal household effects.
mcqs.explanation: Section 28(1)(d) specifically allows the amount paid on account of current repairs to the premises, not being in the nature of capital expenditure, when occupied otherwise than as a tenant. Capital expenditure is explicitly barred, and notional rent or personal insurance is not covered.

mcqs.question: Under Section 28(2), what occurs if machinery or plant is not wholly and exclusively used for the business or profession?
options: The entire deduction claimed under sub-section (1) is disallowed automatically.
A flat 50% statutory reduction applies regardless of actual usage.
The deduction is restricted to the fair proportionate part determined by the Assessing Officer having regard to usage.
The assessee must treat the entire expense as capital expenditure.
mcqs.explanation: Section 28(2) provides that where an asset is partly used or not wholly and exclusively used for business or profession, the deduction under sub-section (1) is restricted to the fair proportionate part determined by the Assessing Officer having regard to its usage.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an allowable deduction in respect of business premises under Section 28(1)(b)?
options: Penalties imposed under town planning regulations.
Advance income-tax paid on commercial profits.
Special assessment fees for capital asset construction.
Land revenue, local rates or municipal taxes paid.
mcqs.explanation: Section 28(1)(b) explicitly allows a deduction for 'land revenue, local rates or municipal taxes paid'. The other options are not listed in Section 28(1)(b).

mcqs.question: What type of insurance premium is allowable as a deduction under Section 28(1)(a)?
options: Premium paid in respect of insurance against risk of damage or destruction of premises, machinery, plant or furniture.
Premium paid on keyman life insurance policies for business partners.
Premium paid to insure against anticipated loss of business profits.
Premium paid to cover bad debt defaults by trade customers.
mcqs.explanation: Section 28(1)(a) specifies that deduction is allowed for any premium paid in respect of insurance against risk of damage or destruction of the premises, machinery, plant or furniture used for the business or profession.

mnemonics.tip: Use PMPF to remember the four specific business assets eligible for deductions under Section 28(1).
